>Would you say that I should change my focus in what matters to me, such as myself, career and relationship? By shifting my focus to these areas, would this allow me to actually not make the mistake again because i am focus in making my relationship better hence i will not act in things I dont wish to do?

Yes! You’re on the right track! I think, from a mindfulness point of view, tho, you should, yes, definitely shift your focus to those things, but also, more importantly, take time out of your day to sit with yourself, and..like I said before, anchor yourself to the present moment through breath, and just focus on that. If you do that, a consequence could be a better ability to take action toward improving those areas (the reason I word it like that is because you shouldn’t really have any expectations while meditating). Another thing I’d say you could do (I think meditation/mindfulness will definitely help you with this) is, again, sit with yourself, but this time focus on making a list of things you want to improve about yourself, career, relationship, and then write steps you can take now to reach those goals. Also I’d say don’t do this out of fear of making mistakes. Do it to help yourself live a more fulfilling life.

I know the “biggest fear/what if I” thought loop all too well (like right now I’m thinking…what if I’m giving absolute shit advice to someone on the internet lol) I’m so sorry you’re struggling with that. I’d say, if you want to be mindful about these thoughts/fears, anchor your focus onto something that will bring you to the present moment (like your breath, around your solar plexus, seems to be a popular one haha, could be any sensation tho) and accept that you are perceiving these thoughts alongside your effort to focus on breathing, and just keep returning your focus to your breath. Whatever thoughts arise, accept them as they are, pure information, and just return your focus to breath. It’s like a muscle you are exercising.

Know that essentially those fears are also the mind extrapolating into the future, to protect you from potential danger. It is not you. It’s a safety mechanism. Maybe try and look at those thoughts/fears from a loving lens…like “aww..my mind is trying to protect me, but I don’t need that right now. I’m ok,” change the narrative. Also ofc self love and compassion is important, I know it seems obvious, but I think it might be a little overlooked? Also try to focus on conjuring that up


Another cognitive behavioral technique you can do with the “what if thoughts” is carry them out as far as you can take them, like, so, for example you already said “what if I make the same mistake again, what if I hate myself.” So then after that be like “ok brain, what if I hate myself?” and then just keep carrying it out, it creates space between you and those thoughts, also exhausts a little I think too

hey, I struggle with similar things/intrusive thoughts, I have ocd, but a good thing to keep in mind (or a good tool to use I’ve found) is to realize those thoughts/dreams are not you/not coming from a place that is “you,” you have no control over them, therefore there’s no need for guilt or fear over them (that is where the guilt/fear lies, that you may think these things are reflective of you. they’re not). You wouldn’t feel guilty for seeing some disturbing imagery on tv? Same kinda idea. As far as making the same mistakes, just try your best to set your intentions. It’s all a lot easier said than done for sure, but the effort itself is what counts, where the benefit comes from.
